title: The ULTIMATE Back/Traps Exercises Tier-List (Leonidas-tier to Shrimp-tier)
summary: NH ranks traps and upper-back exercises from Leonidas tier (named for Alpha Destiny) to Shrimp tier. His main point is that traps grow from holding, catching and stretching heavy weight, not from range of motion or strict form. Top picks: above-knee rack pulls, power shrugs, farmer's carries, hang snatch pulls, Kroc rows, trap bar shrugs and chest-supported incline shrugs.
claims: Traps are an underestimated and misunderstood muscle; the list covers rhomboids and the whole yoke, not only shrugs
Tier name honors Alexander Leonidas (Alpha Destiny), who popularized trap training on YouTube
Deadlift is only decent for traps: lower back, glutes and hamstrings limit it, though years of heavy pulls do build big traps and upper backs
The traps do the same thing throughout a deadlift (stretch under load); range of motion matters for the posterior chain, not the traps
For traps, more weight held is generally better than more range of motion
Above-the-knee rack pull is Leonidas tier: nearly double the deadlift load, so roughly double the trap work
Face pulls can be modified to load the traps with more weight; decent tier, better stimulus-to-fatigue than the deadlift
Overhead press is Shrimp tier for traps; shrugging at the top is a gimmick; overhead shrugs are mediocre
The trap's main function is to stretch and catch weight held in the hands, not overhead stabilization
Dumbbell shrugs are only decent because dumbbells cap the load, even if they put the shoulder in a comfortable neutral position
Snatch-grip shrugs are excellent: more mid traps, upright so no lower-back fatigue, though the wide grip limits load
Power shrugs are Leonidas tier: explode up and catch heavy weight; slow strict tempo shrugs are detrimental for trap growth
Keep the torso vertical on power shrugs; do not hip-hinge
Overhead carries are Shrimp tier: the traps only stabilize passively
Dumbbell farmer's carries are only decent because grip and dumbbell weight limit them; frame holds are excellent
Farmer's carries with a frame and straps are the best trap exercise: heavy load, and every step forces the traps to stretch and contract quickly to stabilize the shoulders
Strongmen have massive traps from heavy pulls and holds
Dumbbell/kettlebell snatch is mediocre; power clean is decent; hang clean pull is excellent; hang snatch pull is Leonidas tier (personal preference)
On hang pulls, pulling to the belly button is enough; pulling higher brings in shoulders, which helps weightlifting but not trap hypertrophy
Upright row is mediocre for traps: essentially a strict hang snatch pull with less weight and more shoulders
Rows with flared elbows recruit more upper back; tucked elbows recruit more lats
Pendlay row is decent for traps because there is no controlled negative and no dangling stretch
Kroc rows are Leonidas tier: body English and catching a dumbbell in front of the body hit the whole upper back
Cable shrugs are Shrimp tier because the cable removes the catch and stretch
Behind-the-back barbell shrugs/curls are excellent for mid and lower traps, but some shoulders dislike them
The trap bar is Leonidas tier for shrugs, power shrugs and carries; bars in front hit more mid back, trap bar more upper traps
Pull-ups are mediocre for traps; shrugs in a pull-up position are Shrimp tier
Feeling or seeing the traps during a lift does not make it a good trap exercise; judge by the muscle's function
Lateral raises and bent-over lateral raises are mediocre for traps; they are shoulder exercises
Reeves incline row is Shrimp, Reeves deadlift mediocre, Reeves shrug decent; snatch-grip shrugs with straps beat them
Reverse snow angels are Shrimp tier
Smith machine shrugs are decent; belt squat machine shrugs are excellent
Chest-supported incline shrugs are Leonidas tier: the stationary body maximizes trap stimulus, heavy dumbbells with straps, and adjusting the incline targets each area
Band pull-aparts are Shrimp tier for traps but good for shoulder health; kettlebell swings are mediocre
Rear-delt ring rows with a rope are decent; reverse ring flies are mediocre
All top-tier trap lifts emphasize the stretch under heavy load; perfect-form 50 lb dumbbell shrugs will never build big traps
exercises: decent for traps; posterior chain limits
Leonidas tier; near double the load
